## Lab updates

### September 2026 · The MCN Lab is recruiting

We are seeking two postdoctoral researchers interested in cognitive computational neuroscience and multimodal approaches to understanding the human brain. [Learn more about the opportunities](join.qmd).

### August 2026 · New review of visual-to-memory transformations

A new review proposes a computational framework for how the brain transforms visual feature codes into sparse, concept-based representations in the medial temporal lobe. [Read the review](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neubiorev.2026.106782).

### February 2026 · New study of visual object coding

A new *Nature Communications* study integrates intracranial EEG, human single-neuron recordings, and computational modeling to characterize how visual object information is transformed across the human temporal lobe. [Read the paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68954-8).

### August 2025 · Brain cells link facial features with identity

Research led by Runnan Cao identified neurons that bridge visual facial features with identity representations and memory. The work appeared in *Nature Human Behaviour*. [Read the WashU research story](https://neuroscienceresearch.wustl.edu/researchers-identify-brain-cells-key-to-facial-recognition/).

### September 2026 · Website launch

Welcome to the new website of the Multimodal Cognitive Neuroscience Lab at Washington University in St. Louis.
